Topics · Hard times

How does God see me, beyond all the debates?

No persuading here. Only how this book sees a human being: honoured, trusted, near, never too late.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلْنَـٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَـٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ وَفَضَّلْنَـٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:70

Translation

what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him? For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor. You make him ruler over the works of your hands. You have put all things under his feet:

﴿فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ سَـٰجِدِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Quran · Al-Hijr 15:29

Translation

Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּיצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֗ם עָפָר֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וַיִּפַּ֥ח בְּאַפָּ֖יו נִשְׁמַ֣ת חַיִּ֑ים וַֽיְהִ֥י הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְנֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּֽה׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 2:7

World English Bible

Yes. This page proves nothing and asks for nothing. Nobody is keeping score. It describes one way of seeing a human being, and you can take it or leave it. In this way of seeing, you were honoured before you did anything. Not for your faith, your family or your record. For being one of the children of Adam. And there is said to be something in a human being that came from beyond the clay: a breath.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer[1528] to him than [his] jugular vein.

Translator's notes

[1528] In absolute knowledge of everything about him. "We" has also been interpreted to mean the angels who are mentioned in the following verse.

Quran · Qaf 50:16

Translation

You are near, Yahweh. All your commandments are truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 119:151

World English Bible

﴿يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ ۚ وَخُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ ضَعِيفًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And Allāh wants to lighten for you [your difficulties]; and mankind was created weak.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:28

Translation

For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.

Original · Hebrew

כִּי־ה֖וּא יָדַ֣ע יִצְרֵ֑נוּ זָ֝כ֗וּר כִּי־עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

the Psalms · 103:14

World English Bible

Two more things, in the same spirit. You are known, and you may pray to Him directly. No fee, no rank, no standing is required: nearer to you, it says, than your own neck vein. And your weakness is allowed for. A human being was made weak. That is said as a plain fact, in a sentence about wanting to lighten the load. For someone who has been told only what they fall short of, it can be strange to hear that the shortfall was known from the start.

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

﴿فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا٥ إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease [i.e., relief]. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

Quran · Ash-Sharh 94:5-6

Translation

Yahweh my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me. Yahweh, you have brought up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit. Sing praise to Yahweh, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name. For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

Original · Hebrew

יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֑י שִׁוַּ֥עְתִּי אֵ֝לֶ֗יךָ וַתִּרְפָּאֵֽנִי׃ יְֽהוָ֗ה הֶֽעֱלִ֣יתָ מִן־שְׁא֣וֹל נַפְשִׁ֑י חִ֝יִּיתַ֗נִי מִיָּֽרְדִי־בֽוֹר׃ זַמְּר֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חֲסִידָ֑יו וְ֝הוֹד֗וּ לְזֵ֣כֶר קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ כִּ֤י רֶ֨גַע ׀ בְּאַפּוֹ֮ חַיִּ֪ים בִּרְצ֫וֹנ֥וֹ בָּ֭עֶרֶב יָלִ֥ין בֶּ֗כִי וְלַבֹּ֥קֶר רִנָּֽה׃

the Psalms · 30:2-5

World English Bible

The last thing is hope. This verse is addressed to people who have gone far against themselves, and what it forbids is despair. Another sentence says one short thing twice: with hardship comes ease. Neither sets a date, and neither makes pain small. This page does not argue for them here. It says only that a person can be offered them, and that the same book contains severe pages too, which are stated elsewhere. You have seen what it can say at its gentlest.

A question for you

Would you like to go on to something, or leave it here?

If you sayI'll leave it here.
ThenGood. Nothing is waiting for you.
If you sayI'd like to know how a person speaks to Him, if they do.
ThenThere is a short page on that, with no conditions and no ritual.
If you sayI still want answers, but quietly.
ThenAs you wish. Here is a way to test things yourself, at your own pace.

The same in the other books
